passages.title: Dialogue 1: The new shopping centre
passages.text:
Man: Have you been to the new shopping centre yet?
Woman: Yes, I went on Saturday. Everyone told me it would be really crowded, but actually it was fine. I didn't have to queue anywhere.
Man: And what are the shops like?
Woman: Well, that's the thing. They're the same big chain stores you find in every town. I was hoping for some smaller, independent places, you know, something a bit different. So it was a bit disappointing, really.
Man: What about parking? That's always a nightmare in town.
Woman: Oh, that was great. It's free for the first three hours, and there were loads of spaces.

passages.title: Dialogue 2: Taking a jacket back
passages.text:
Woman: Are you taking that jacket back to the shop? I thought you loved it.
Man: I do. The colour's great, and it fits me perfectly.
Woman: So what's the problem? Did you decide it was too expensive?
Man: No, it was actually in the sale, so it was a real bargain. But look at this. The zip's broken already, and I've only worn it twice.
Woman: Oh, that's annoying. Have you still got the receipt?
Man: Yes, luckily. I'm hoping they'll just give me a new one.

passages.title: Dialogue 3: The Sunday market
passages.text:
Woman: The Sunday market was much bigger than I expected, wasn't it?
Man: Yes, there were loads of stalls. The clothes were a bit disappointing, though. It was mostly cheap T-shirts.
Woman: Really? I didn't think so. I found a lovely wool scarf for five pounds. But the food stalls were amazing.
Man: Absolutely. They were the best thing there. That Thai curry I had was fantastic.
Woman: I know. I'd go back just for the food, to be honest.

passages.title: Dialogue 4: A new phone
passages.text:
Girl: Dad, could you give me a lift into town on Saturday morning?
Dad: What for? Is it for that new phone? You know it's cheaper if you buy it online.
Girl: I know, and I'm not going to buy it in the shop. I'll order it online when I get home. I just want to see it properly first, and hold it in my hand. It looks quite big in the photos, and I want to check it'll fit in my pocket.
Dad: That's sensible. OK, I'll drive you in after breakfast.

passages.title: Dialogue 5: The post office
passages.text:
Woman: Did you see the post office has changed its opening hours? It's open until seven on weekdays now.
Man: Yes, I saw the notice.
Woman: Were you surprised?
Man: Not really. People had been asking for longer hours for ages. But it makes such a difference to me. I could never get there before five because of work, so I had to send all my parcels on Saturdays, and the queue was always awful.
Woman: I thought you'd be annoyed, because it's closed on Saturday afternoons now.
Man: That doesn't matter to me any more. I can just go on my way home.

passages.title: Dialogue 6: A hairdresser
passages.text:
Man: I really need a haircut, but I hated what the last place did to me.
Woman: You should try Sam's on Bridge Street. I've been going there for years.
Man: Is it cheap?
Woman: Not especially. It's about the same as everywhere else. And you have to book at least a week ahead, because it's always busy.
Man: So why do you like it so much?
Woman: Because they actually listen to you. They ask exactly what you want before they start cutting, and you come out looking the way you asked. That's rare, believe me.

questions.question: You will hear two friends talking about a new shopping centre. What does the woman think about it?
options: a) It is difficult to find a place to park there.
b) It is too busy and crowded at weekends.
c) The shops are the same as in other towns.
questions.explanation: She says the shops are "the same big chain stores you find in every town" and she was hoping for "something a bit different", so she was disappointed. It was not crowded ("actually it was fine") and parking "was great".

questions.question: You will hear a man talking to a friend about a jacket. Why is he taking it back to the shop?
options: a) Part of it is damaged.
b) It is the wrong size.
c) He paid too much for it.
questions.explanation: He says "The zip's broken already, and I've only worn it twice." The size is not the problem because "it fits me perfectly", and the price is not the problem because it was "a real bargain" in the sale.

questions.question: You will hear two friends talking about a market they visited. What do they agree about?
options: a) The food was the best thing there.
b) The clothes were of poor quality.
c) The market was smaller than they expected.
questions.explanation: The woman says "the food stalls were amazing" and the man replies "Absolutely. They were the best thing there." They disagree about the clothes (the woman found a lovely scarf), and the woman says the market was "much bigger" than she expected.

questions.question: You will hear a girl talking to her father. What does she want to do in town on Saturday?
options: a) Buy the new phone in a shop there
b) Find a cheaper price for it online
c) Look at a phone before she buys it
questions.explanation: She says "I'm not going to buy it in the shop"; she just wants "to see it properly first, and hold it in my hand" to check the size. She will order it online later at home, not in town.

questions.question: You will hear two neighbours talking about their local post office. How does the man feel about the new opening hours?
questions.explanation: He says the change "makes such a difference to me" because he can now go on his way home from work instead of queuing on Saturdays. He is "Not really" surprised, and the Saturday closing "doesn't matter to me any more", so he is not annoyed.

questions.question: You will hear a woman recommending a hairdresser to a friend. Why does she like it?
options: a) You can go there without booking ahead.
b) The staff pay attention to customers' wishes.
c) It is cheaper than other hairdressers.
questions.explanation: She likes it "Because they actually listen to you. They ask exactly what you want before they start cutting." It is "about the same" price as everywhere else, and you have to book "at least a week ahead".
